description: The ASPERN rating of one vault: an overall letter (A+ best … D worst) from eight component letters with published weights (control and governance 20, exit liquidity 15, collateral quality 15, on-chain borrower position health 10 (not an assessment of borrower creditworthiness), oracle 10, concentration 10, transparency and data evidence 10, track record 10), each with the inputs and the threshold that set it and the vault-page section that grounds it. Caps are rules and are listed where they applied (sanctions match, impaired market, unbounded control, the published band, a component at D, band withheld, control or exit not rated). A component without a usable reading is not rated, never given a default letter; coverage says how many directly applicable components were read and whether a wrapper’s indirect lending risk (through the vault behind its adapter) was assessed or not fully assessed: indirect is never “does not apply”. Each component carries its applicability (DIRECT_APPLICABLE, DIRECT_NOT_APPLICABLE, INDIRECT_APPLICABLE_ASSESSED, INDIRECT_POSSIBLE_NOT_ASSESSED), its scope (control: partial where other control paths were not fully assessed), reason codes, its sources with their read times, and on the oracle and position health its evidenceStatus (an oracle resting on price agreement alone is conditional or unassessed, its price-agreement letter beside as `conditional`, never the rating); every active cap is listed with the one that binds, and the credit overlay’s state (active, last_assessed, expired, would_trigger, not_run, not_applicable) with its last known verdict and age. Read from the vault’s latest daily stored due-diligence document, whose time, digest and snapshot id come with it, and report.selection says why that document and names the last paid issue where it differs; the overall is never better than that document’s published band allows. A model output over on-chain data: not a credit rating, not a probability of loss. Free.

slug.description: The vault slug or contract address, as list_vaults returns it.

disclaimer.description: Not a credit rating, not a probability of loss, not advice.

meta.description: How current this answer is and what it was read from: `freshness` and the ages behind it. Present on every answer from this server, whatever the tool.

rating.description: methodVersion, reportDigest, snapshotId, reportAsOf, scoredAt; overall (rating, state rated | not_rated, weightedPoints, beforeCaps, caps [{code, ceiling, says}] that lowered it, activeCaps [{code, ceiling, says, binds, lowers}], bindingCap, notRatedBecause, reasonCodes, notCurrent {lastKnownWouldBe, says} where the credit overlay expired or did not run), coverage (rated, applicable, total, ratedWeightShare, directlyApplicable, directlyRated, indirectAssessed, indirectNotAssessed, indirectLending none | assessed | not_fully_assessed, full, says), components [{key, name, weight, state rated | not_rated | not_applicable, applicability, rating, display, scope, scopeSays, restsOn, inputs [{label, value}], rule, says, notRatedBecause, reasonCodes, sources [{id, readAt}], readAt, indirect {paths, assessedShare, says}, dMeans {kind, says} where D, overlay, track (contract age, observation start, reliable share-price days, gaps, downsampling), section {anchor, label}}], band (published, weightedModel, status, ceiling, says), creditOverlay (state, current, triggered, wouldTrigger, lastAssessed, ageHours, lastKnown, reasonCode, says), source (issued | computed_on_read), issuedAs ({version, rating} where the document was issued under an older rating version), says, disclaimer. Null where no due-diligence document is stored.

says.description: The rating in one sentence, with the document it comes from.

warnings.description: Anything the server wants a caller to know about THIS answer before acting on it, each {code, message, says} with message and says the same sentence. Empty is the normal case and is not a guarantee.
